question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Turning Tides: 11th and 12th Centuries Practice Paper

questions.question_text: In which battle did Muhammad Ghuri defeat Prithviraj Chauhan in 1192 CE?
Who wrote 'Kitab al-Hind' after studying Sanskrit and Indian sciences in the 11th century?
The Chola ruler who executed a famous naval campaign against Srivijaya in 1025 CE was:
The mathematical treatise 'Lilavati' was composed in Sanskrit verse by:
Differentiate between the military objectives of Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghuri.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Mahmud of Ghazni (11th C): Plunder raids to extract temple wealth without territorial governance. Muhammad Ghuri (12th C): Permanent territorial conquest and political annexation.

questions.question_text: Name two major merchant guilds that operated overseas trade networks under the Cholas.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Ayyavole (Five Hundred Swamis of Ayyavole).
2. Manigramam.

questions.question_text: Analyze why the 11th and 12th centuries represent a major period of transition ('Turning Tides') in Indian history.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Transition across two fronts: 1. North India: Turkic invasions dismantled Rajput polities, founding Islamic rule culminating in the Delhi Sultanate. 2. Peninsular India: Zenith of Chola maritime naval power, overseas trade, monumental Dravida/Nagara architecture, and major advancements in mathematics.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: A relief frieze at Khajuraho's Lakshmana Temple depicts a 12th-century military army.
(a) What four divisions ('Chaturanga') of the military are depicted?
(b) Which dynasty built Khajuraho's Kandariya Mahadeva temple?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Infantry (swords/shields), Archery, Cavalry, and War Elephants.
(b) Chandella Dynasty.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Turning Tides: 11th and 12th Centuries Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Mahmud of Ghazni conducted his famous plunder raid on the Somnath Temple in which year?
The famous Brihadishvara Temple in Thanjavur was built by which Chola king?
Which mountain pass served as the primary historic invasion route into North-West India?
The Sun Temple at Konark, designed as a giant stone chariot, was built by:
Describe the objective approach used by Al-Biruni in writing 'Kitab al-Hind'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit, consulted Hindu scholars directly, cited Indian astronomical/philosophical texts, and compared Indian social customs with Greek and Islamic systems without partisan bias.

questions.question_text: What was the significance of Rajendra I constructing the new capital Gangaikonda Cholapuram?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Built to celebrate his victorious military expedition to the Ganga River in the North; featured a grand temple and massive irrigation reservoir (Cholagangam).

questions.question_text: Examine the impact of military raids on central monastic universities (Nalanda/Vikramashila) and how knowledge survived.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Impact: Burning of irreplaceable manuscript libraries (Dharmaganja) and dispersal of scholar networks.
Survival: Knowledge persisted via decentralized regional courts, temple math schools, palm-leaf copies carried to Nepal/Tibet, and family scholar lineages.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: The Konark Sun Temple features 24 stone wheels.
(a) What astronomical function do these wheels serve?
(b) How many horses draw this stone chariot?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) The wheels function as precise sundials calculating time based on shadow angles.
(b) Drawn by 7 carved stone horses representing days of the week.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Turning Tides: 11th and 12th Centuries Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Who won the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 CE?
The Hoysala dynasty built intricately carved stellate (star-shaped) temples at:
Which Srivijaya maritime territory was conquered during Rajendra I's naval campaign?
'Siddhanta Shiromani' is a masterwork on astronomy and mathematics written by:
Explain why Chola merchant guilds maintained private armed contingents.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Merchant guilds like Ayyavole operated international overland and maritime trade routes; armed contingents protected valuable trade caravans from piracy and bandits.

questions.question_text: What topics are covered in Bhaskaracharya II's mathematical text 'Lilavati'?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Arithmetic, geometry, permutations, combinations, quadratic equations, and interest calculations posed in poetic Sanskrit riddles.

questions.question_text: Detail the architectural and structural features of Chola temple art as seen in Brihadishvara Temple.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Tower (Vimana): 13-tiered 216-foot pyramidal tower topped by a 80-ton monolithic stone cupola.
2. Enclosure: Massive stone boundary walls with sculpted Gopurams.
3. Monoliths: Single-stone colossal Nandi bull statue and bronze lost-wax casting sculptures (Nataraja).

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: Al-Biruni observes Indian mathematics in 'Kitab al-Hind'.
(a) Which Indian mathematical concept particularly impressed Al-Biruni?
(b) In which language did Al-Biruni compose his book?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) The decimal place-value system and the mathematical concept of Zero.
(b) Arabic.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Turning Tides: 11th and 12th Centuries Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho belongs to which architectural style?
Which Paramara king of Malwa was a renowned scholar who built the Bhojeshwar Temple?
Chola naval ships navigated across which sea body to reach Srivijaya?
The Hindu Shahi kingdom ruled over which region before Ghaznavid invasions?
Explain how Chola bronze sculptures were made using the 'lost-wax' (cire perdue) process.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A wax model is sculpted, covered in clay, and heated so wax drains out. Molten bronze is poured into the hollow mold; once cooled, the clay shell is broken revealing solid metal.

questions.question_text: What were the consequences of the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE)?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Broke Rajput military resistance in North India, established Ghurid administrative control over Delhi and Ajmer, opening the way for the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question_text: Examine the role of Chola naval power in securing Indian Ocean trade routes and establishing cultural links with Southeast Asia.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rajendra I built a formidable navy to defeat Srivijaya pirates who blockaded trade routes. Securing the Malacca Strait enabled direct Chola trade with China and spread Tamil merchant inscriptions, Hindu/Buddhist architecture, and rituals across Southeast Asia.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: A math problem in 'Lilavati' asks a riddle about a flock of swans.
(a) Why did Bhaskara II compose math problems in poetic verse?
(b) What branch of mathematics covers permutations and combination riddles?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) To make mathematical learning engaging, memorable, and accessible for students through oral recitation.
(b) Combinatorics.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Turning Tides: 11th and 12th Centuries Practice Paper

questions.question_text: The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur was constructed under which regional dynasty?
Prithviraj Chauhan belonged to which Rajput ruling dynasty?
Which Chola emperor built the Brihadishvara Temple at Thanjavur?
Al-Biruni accompanied which invader to India?
Describe the features of Vesara architectural style seen in Karnataka temples.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Vesara style is a hybrid architectural tradition combining Northern Nagara tower profiles with Southern Dravida wall plans and star-shaped platforms.

questions.question_text: What was the strategic importance of controlling the Khyber Pass in medieval times?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Khyber Pass served as the primary northwestern gateway through the Hindu Kush mountains, controlling military invasion routes and overland trade caravans into India.

questions.question_text: Provide a comprehensive survey of major temple construction achievements across India in the 11th and 12th centuries.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Cholas (Tamil Nadu): Brihadishvara (Dravida) — massive Vimana and bronze sculptures.
2. Chandellas (Bundelkhand): Kandariya Mahadeva (Nagara) — soaring mountain-like Shikharas.
3. Eastern Gangas (Odisha): Konark Sun Temple (Kalinga) — chariot architecture.
4. Hoysalas (Karnataka): Belur/Halebidu (Vesara) — intricate soapstone carvings.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: A Chola inscription records an 'Ayyavole' guild charter.
(a) What goods did merchant guilds trade internationally?
(b) How did guilds support temple construction?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Spices, textiles, horses, elephant tusks, precious stones, and metals.
(b) Guilds donated trade profits, endowed lamps, and commissioned bronze icons and temple halls.
